name: Explicit Operator-Controlled Live Model Invocation Boundary
objective: Graduate the bounded GENERATE model-source-authoring path into an explicitly operator-controlled live invocation boundary that composes the existing hardened OpenAI-compatible transport, bounded model source-authoring provider, and authoritative generateIntentRiverDev command while requiring explicit operator authorization, accepting endpoint and model as explicit operator inputs, receiving the credential through standard input rather than command-line arguments or ambient secret discovery, returning only the validated in-memory implementation intent to standard output, and preserving all existing repository mutation, proposal approval, manifest generation, execution, commit, push, deployment, governance, context-externalization, and transport-security boundaries.
commitMessage: GENERATE-004: Add explicit operator-controlled live model invocation boundary

generationContract.composition: The operator-controlled command validates explicit live-invocation authorization and required non-secret inputs, receives the credential through standard input, constructs the existing OpenAI-compatible transport with caller-supplied endpoint/model/credential, wraps that transport with the existing bounded model source-authoring provider, and invokes the existing generateIntentRiverDev authoritative generation command.
generationContract.credentialBoundary: The credential must not be accepted as a positional argument, CLI flag value, environment variable, dotenv value, repository file, configuration file, or arbitrary secret-store lookup. It is supplied explicitly for the invocation through standard input, kept in memory only for construction of the existing transport, never intentionally echoed, serialized, persisted, or included in errors, and is not written into generated intent output.
generationContract.authorizationBoundary: The live model network request may occur only when the operator has supplied the exact explicit live-invocation authorization flag defined by GENERATE-004. Absence of that authorization must fail closed before credential consumption or network invocation.
generationContract.networkBoundary: All model network activity must continue exclusively through the existing GENERATE-002/003 OpenAI-compatible transport. GENERATE-004 may compose that transport but must not add fetch logic, alternate HTTP clients, shell networking, or a second transport boundary.
generationContract.generationBoundary: The existing generateIntentRiverDev command remains authoritative for repository-root identity, governed plan/specification paths, architecture-grounded context creation, branch identity, GENERATE-001 governance, provider invocation, deterministic implementation-intent construction, and final intent validation.
generationContract.outputBoundary: Successful execution prints only the validated generated implementation intent through the existing intent formatting contract. GENERATE-004 does not write an intent file or any other repository artifact.
generationContract.mutationBoundary: GENERATE-004 performs no repository source/content mutation, generated-artifact persistence, proposal generation or approval, manifest generation, execution, commit, push, deployment, or authority creation.
generationContract.scopeBoundary: The model cannot choose or broaden target paths. Target decisions remain exclusively derived from the authoritative plan and existing GENERATE-001 governance.

acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated GENERATE-004 operator command composes the existing hardened transport, bounded model source-authoring provider, and authoritative generateIntentRiverDev path without duplicating their governance or security responsibilities.
Live network invocation fails closed unless an exact explicit operator live-invocation authorization signal is present.
Missing or invalid plan path, specification path, endpoint, model, authorization, or credential fails closed.
The credential is not accepted through command-line arguments and is not discovered from process.env, dotenv files, repository files, or arbitrary secret stores.
The operator boundary reads the credential from standard input only after non-secret command arguments and explicit authorization have been validated.
The credential is not intentionally printed, formatted into generated intent, persisted, or disclosed by GENERATE-004 errors.
Remote HTTPS and explicit loopback-local HTTP behavior remain governed by the unchanged GENERATE-003 transport.
The existing governed model-facing context projection remains unchanged and authoritative.

The existing generateIntentRiverDev command remains authoritative for plan loading, governed repository paths, architecture-grounded development context, branch matching, generation governance, and implementation-intent validation.
Successful operator invocation returns only the validated in-memory implementation intent to standard output.
No intent persistence, proposal generation, proposal approval, manifest generation, repository mutation, execution authorization, Git authority, commit, push, or deployment is introduced.
Tests use fake transport/fetch or controlled stdin seams and perform no live external network request and use no real credential.
Existing GENERATE-001, GENERATE-002, GENERATE-003, downstream proposal lifecycle, and historical manually authored implementation-intent behavior remain compatible.
approvalBoundaries: Only an explicit human/operator invocation of the GENERATE-004 live command may authorize its single bounded live model request.

The live-invocation authorization signal authorizes only the model request needed to generate candidate content; it creates no repository mutation, proposal approval, manifest, execution, commit, push, or deployment authority.
The model credential may not be supplied as a command-line argument or discovered from ambient environment variables, dotenv files, repository files, or arbitrary secret stores.
The credential must not be intentionally echoed, persisted, serialized into implementation intent, or included in command errors.
Network access remains confined to the unchanged OpenAI-compatible transport and retains GENERATE-003 remote HTTPS enforcement.
No model output may select paths, broaden scope, mutate the repository, approve proposals, create manifests, authorize execution, invoke Git, commit, push, or deploy.
The existing generateIntentRiverDev boundary remains authoritative for governed planning, repository context, branch identity, implementation-intent generation, and final validation.
Successful GENERATE-004 execution stops after returning the validated in-memory implementation intent to standard output.
